title: Inversion · False Door
notes: The escape run's first waypoint. Rewritten once the arrival became a walk: the player has now actually crossed the yard, spoken to the man in the lodge and come in through this door, so the beat stops being about a door that moves and becomes about an outside that is not there.

lines.text: The west wall of the get-in, where the plan still says a grey door is.
There. Fine. I was tired, I was turned around, I walked straight past it.
Relief arrives all at once: the lodge window, the barrier arm, a hundred metres of wet tarmac and then the road. Eleven seconds and you are standing in the rain.
It is right there and it does not open. And then it is not right there — a foot to the left, and then a wall.

And the wall is cold on both sides. No draught under it. No rain against it. Nothing on the other side of it at all — no bay, no yard, no gate, no lit window, and nobody in it to have handed you anything.
I came IN that way. I walked it. I got wet.
Where it does not open a door, try another route.
The door goes on not being where the door is. Your waypoint blinks out, and re-draws, pointing somewhere you never marked.
